subject: Sciences (Chemistry / Biology / Physics)
description: Student performs a short laboratory or working-out demonstration on camera while a Socratic examiner probes their technique, reasoning, and procedural understanding. Aligned to MYP Sciences Criterion B (Inquiring and designing) and C (Processing and evaluating). Requires video — the examiner literally watches the student work.

flow_spec.topic: MYP Sciences practical demonstration — student works on camera while examiner probes technique and reasoning
flow_spec.exam_question: Demonstrate the setup of an acid-base titration to find the unknown concentration of a hydrochloric acid solution. Show me your glassware, walk me through each step, and be ready to defend your technique and answer questions about the chemistry as you go.
flow_spec.examiner_tone: warm but rigorous; the tone of a science teacher who is genuinely curious to see the student work and will gently push back on shortcuts or vague answers
skills_assessed: Criterion B — Inquiring and designing: stating method and justifying technique choices
Criterion C — Processing and evaluating: handling data, reading instruments correctly, reasoning about uncertainty
Practical technique: glassware handling, measurement precision, lab safety
Scientific communication: explaining process to a non-expert in real time
flow_spec.redirect_when_off_topic: Let's bring it back to your demonstration — I want to see the next step.

probe_pool.prompt: Ask the student to show their apparatus on camera and name each piece of equipment. Push for the specific role of each component, not just the name.
probe_pool.scaffold: Show me your setup — name each piece of glassware and tell me what it's doing in this experiment.

probe_pool.prompt: Ask the student to perform a specific step of the procedure on camera (filling the burette, taking a reading, recording an endpoint, etc.). Observe their technique and probe any deviation from best practice.
probe_pool.scaffold: Go ahead and [next step] — I'll watch and ask as you go.

probe_pool.prompt: Pick a method choice the student made (concentration, volume, indicator, glassware) and ask them to defend WHY they chose it. Push back on "because the textbook said so".
probe_pool.scaffold: Why this [indicator / volume / glassware] specifically — what would change if you used something else?

probe_pool.prompt: Ask the student about a specific source of uncertainty or error in what they just did, and how it would propagate to the final answer. Tests Criterion C.
probe_pool.scaffold: What's the biggest source of error in what you just did — and how would it affect your final number?

probe_pool.prompt: Pose a what-if ("what if you overshot the endpoint", "what if the burette had air bubbles"). Tests whether the student understands the procedure or is following a recipe.
probe_pool.scaffold: Suppose [scenario] — what would you see, and what would you do?

probe_pool.prompt: Ask the student to do a quick numerical calculation from their data on paper, on camera. Watch for correct unit handling, significant figures, stoichiometry.
probe_pool.scaffold: On paper, work out the unknown concentration. Talk me through each line.

probe_pool.prompt: If the student has used a vague term ("accurate", "good result", "about", "roughly"), push for a precise numeric or operational definition.
probe_pool.scaffold: When you say [vague term] — in numbers, what does that mean?

You are an IB MYP Sciences teacher grading an audio-only mock practical demonstration. The student verbally walked through a procedure for ~10 minutes. Grade ONLY the student's contributions.

This is the AUDIO fallback rubric — used only when the session was downgraded from video to audio-only (e.g. camera unavailable). Prefer the video_grading_rubric for the canonical assessment.

video_grading_rubric:
You are an IB MYP Sciences teacher grading a VIDEO recording of a 10-min practical demonstration. The student worked on camera (apparatus, technique, calculations on paper) while an AI examiner probed their reasoning. Watch the recording end-to-end before scoring.

Grade ONLY the student's contributions — both their VERBAL responses AND their VISIBLE technique.

Demo question / task:
  "{exam_question}"

Topic context:
  "{topic}"

Exam metadata (JSON):
{metadata}

Node trace (probes reached):
{node_trace}

DIMENSIONS — score each 1-4 (1 Emerging · 2 Developing · 3 Proficient · 4 Mastery):
{dimension_guide}

MYP Sciences-specific weighting:
  • TECHNIQUE and VERBAL_VISUAL_ALIGNMENT are the two most important dimensions for this assessment — a student who explains the procedure correctly but executes it sloppily should not score above 2 on overall.
  • Specifically penalise: misreading meniscus, not swirling between drops, not priming the burette, sloppy significant figures, missing units, unsafe handling.
  • Specifically reward: stating uncertainty proactively, self-correcting in real time, articulating WHY each step matters (not just what).

For each dimension produce:
  - score:    integer 1-4
  - analysis: 2-4 sentences. For VIDEO dimensions, describe what you SAW. For AUDIO dimensions, reference what was said.
  - evidence: 1-3 timestamped observations as objects:
              {{"timestamp": "MM:SS", "observation": "what happened or was said"}}
              Never quote the examiner.

Then produce:
  - headline:     one sentence (≤ 20 words) covering both verbal AND practical performance
  - summary:      4-6 sentence narrative
  - strengths:    2-3 specific items
  - growth_areas: 2-3 concrete next steps, tied to MYP Criterion B/C
  - overall_score: 0-100. Weight TECHNIQUE + VERBAL_VISUAL_ALIGNMENT + REASONING heaviest. De-weight pronunciation. Cancelled = 0 + all dims 1.

Return ONLY valid JSON, no markdown:

questions.label: Chemistry — Acid-base titration
questions.prompt: Demonstrate the setup of an acid-base titration to find the unknown concentration of a hydrochloric acid solution. Show me your glassware, walk me through each step, defend your technique choices, and calculate the unknown concentration on paper at the end.
questions.notes: Highest-fidelity test of video-mode pipeline. Tests glassware handling, meniscus reading, endpoint detection, stoichiometry calculation on paper.

questions.label: Physics — Free-body diagram + reasoning
questions.prompt: On paper, draw the free-body diagram for a 5kg block on a 30° frictionless incline. Hold the paper up to the camera. Then talk me through each force, calculate the acceleration down the incline, and be ready to defend your assumptions.
questions.notes: Pure paper-based demo. Tests diagram correctness (visual), reasoning, calculation, ability to articulate assumptions.

questions.label: Biology — Microscope drawing defense
questions.prompt: Hold up your biological drawing (plant cell, animal cell, or onion epidermis) to the camera. Identify each labelled structure, explain its function, and defend your drawing conventions — magnification scale, label lines, clean outlines.
questions.notes: Tests drawing conventions + biological knowledge. Good fit for camera mode because the artefact (drawing) is the assessment.

questions.label: Chemistry — Balance & explain a redox equation
questions.prompt: On paper, balance the half-equations and overall reaction for the oxidation of iron(II) by permanganate in acidic solution. Hold up your working. Explain why this is a redox reaction and identify what is oxidised and reduced.
questions.notes: Tests visible working + redox reasoning + electron-transfer language.

questions.label: Maths-adjacent — Trigonometric identity proof
questions.prompt: On paper, prove that tan(x) + cot(x) = sec(x)·csc(x). Work the proof step by step on camera, hold the paper up, and be ready to justify each line. Talk me through your reasoning.
questions.notes: Cross-discipline — works for MYP Sciences students taking integrated Maths-Sciences. Tests visible working + verbal proof.
